topic: Cubic smoothing spline: minimize the integral of the squared second derivative subject to a weighted residual constraint
own_question: How to construct an optimal smoothing (non-interpolating) cubic spline for approximate data
actual_method_and_evidence: Variational derivation of a cubic spline with a Lagrange parameter found by Newton iteration from p=0. Includes an ALGOL procedure. Demonstrations: numerical derivatives of sin(x) rounded to four decimals, compared by mean-square error against difference quotients and interpolating splines, and one curve-plotting figure with n=100, S=90. The method is offline, batch and two-sided over the whole data set. It involves no time-series causality, no plasma data and no forecasting.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Smoothing splines trade fidelity to noisy ordinates, weighted by per-point uncertainty, against curvature. Setting the smoothing level to zero recovers cubic spline interpolation.
claim_checks.qualification: Applies to a fitted curve over all points (two-sided). It is relevant only as background if a two-sided interpolation or spline reference is discussed.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not applicable. Uses all data points simultaneously, so it is noncausal by construction.
validation_if_relevant: Single synthetic example (rounded sin table) plus one illustrative plot. No held-out validation.
forbidden_inferences: That our two-sided interpolation baseline is Reinsch's spline unless it is actually implemented as one
Any CES, plasma or KSTAR relevance
Generalizing it as representative of all prior smoothing work
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Cite only if the paper describes a spline-based two-sided reference or smoothing step. Otherwise exclude, because it does not address causal nowcasting or diagnostics.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
